description: Sections from any site that look and read like the given ones, by their screenshots and what they show. Use it to widen from hits you liked, or to find alternatives to a section you have. What is like the ones you liked includes ones you've seen: pass every key you've been shown as exclude_keys. q steers it ("like these but light"); roles, sites, page, contains and categories filter it, exclude_categories leaves out kinds of site, and exclude_sites and exclude_keys leave out what you have already seen. It answers like search_sections (same fields, and include adds the same bigger ones), in one group of kind "similar". Not for a description alone: search_sections takes that, and its like does the same with a query.

categories.description: Only sections from sites of these kinds, as regards.design files every site: ai, agency, portfolio, personal, saas, startup, product, technology, finance, fashion, ecommerce, editorial, books, art, photography, architecture, music, food-drink, health, education, entertainment, web3, crypto, resource. E.g. ["saas", "ai", "product"] for software and AI products only. Use it when the user wants references from a kind of site (a sector, "only SaaS and AI sites"), not to describe what they are designing. A site you name keeps its own group whatever its kind; applied.categories says what was kept to.

contains.description: Only sections that visibly show this text, as whole words (case, accents and punctuation ignored), e.g. "Get started" or "pricing": the exact phrase in a heading or large type ranks first, then smaller mentions, then sections with all its words apart. Alone it lists them; with q it filters that search. A q that starts with "CONTAINS:" does the same with the text after it; quotes in any other q are just part of the query. Each hit's match.text marks where it is.

diversity.description: 'site': at most one section per site, for the widest spread (default: at most two). A site you name keeps its own.

exclude_categories.description: Leave out sections from sites of these kinds (the same names as categories), e.g. ["agency", "portfolio", "fashion"] for no design studios, agencies, portfolios or fashion brands. They are left out before ranking, so the results still fill limit; applied.excludeCategories says which were.

exclude_keys.description: Leave out these sections ("page/section", hit.key): the ones earlier searches showed, so a search again brings new ones, and the ones turned down, with their other parts and repeats. They are left out before ranking, so the results still fill limit with others.

exclude_sites.description: Leave out these sites (host like "linear.app", a name like "linear", or a page id), e.g. ones that keep coming back. They are left out before ranking, so the results still fill limit from other sites; applied.exclude says which were.

include.description: Which bigger fields each hit carries: "tiles" (images.tiles, its screenshot tiles' URLs; view_section shows the section itself), "geometry" (where it sits on its page, page px) and "page" (the page in full: host, height, shotAt, viewport, dsf, innerScroller). Left out by default; get_section has all of them for one section.

keys.description: Section keys ("page/section") to find more like.

page.description: 'home': only sites' main pages; 'subpage': only other pages.

q.description: Optional: what else the results should be, in any words.

roles.description: Only these kinds of section. Usually leave it out: the query is read for them ("pricing section" → pricing; "header" → hero). Set it to force a filter.

search_id.description: Optional: the searchId of the search you got this from, so we learn which results were useful.

sites.description: Only these sites (host like "linear.app", a name like "linear", or a page id), as if named in the query.

name: similar_sections

applied.description: The filters and seeds actually used.

categories.description: The kinds of site the results keep to (category slugs), when they keep to some: asked for (categories), or read from the query.

contains.description: Text the sections must visibly show (contains, or a query that starts with CONTAINS:).

diversity.description: 'site': at most one result per site.

exclude.description: What was left out of the results (excludeSites, excludeKeys), when anything was.

keys.description: The sections left out, as asked (with their other parts and repeats).

sites.description: The sites left out, as hosts.

excludeCategories.description: The kinds of site left out of the results (category slugs), when any were: asked for (exclude_categories), or read from the query.

hosts.description: Sites the query named that we have.

rolesAs.description: filter: only these kinds of section; prefer: they rank higher.

degraded.description: Set when part of the search was unavailable, so the results may be less precise than usual.

category.description: The kind of site it is from, as regards.design files its site (a category: saas, ai, product, agency, portfolio, fashion, …); null when its site is filed under none.

contains.description: Roles of notable blocks inside it (a hero holding a logo strip).

geometry.description: The section on its page, page px of our capture (left/right: its horizontal crop; blocks: sub-block boundaries; split: one part of a long section). With include "geometry"; get_section and page_sections give it anyway.

tiles.description: Top to bottom; top/height in section px. With include "tiles"; get_section gives them anyway.

sizes.description: The tile at every width it is stored at, px, smallest first; the last is url. get_section only.

key.description: "page/section"; stable until the page is re-cut.

more.description: Results from this site held back by the per-site cap.

parts.description: Other keys collapsed into this result (parts of one long section, repeats).

text.description: When text was asked for (contains, or a q starting with CONTAINS:): where the section shows it, with the matched characters marked and their rects (section px).

exact.description: true: every phrase as written, inside one heading, label or paragraph; false: all its words, apart.

marks.description: The matched characters of text, as [start, end) pairs.

ocr.description: Read from the pixels (text inside an image), not from the page.

rects.description: Where they are in the section, section CSS px (inside one line of text, approximate).

text.description: The heading, label or paragraph the match is in (a snippet of a long one).

via.description: What found it: look (screenshots), details (annotation meaning), words (keywords), text (the text it visibly shows), and boosts (role, motion, novel). The keys of the contract's match.ranks.

motion.description: Whether it moves on the live page, null when nothing was seen to. certainty: measured = recorded moving, likely = only a surface that could move. kind: continuous (keeps moving), cycling (swaps on a timer), reveal (animates in once on scroll).

novelty.description: How unusual against typical sections of its role: 1 template … 5 experimental.

page.description: The page it is on: id, url, title and kind; with include "page" (and in get_section), also host, height, shotAt, viewport, dsf and innerScroller.

kind.description: exact: the named site; match: what was asked; related: the rest of the query without the role filter; similar: looks and reads like the exact/liked sections; browse: no query.

notices.description: Things the caller should know: a named site we do not have yet, a filter that left few results.

searchId.description: This search in our logs. Pass it as search_id to get_section, view_section, page_sections and similar_sections on its results: it tells us which results were useful.

categories.description: The kinds of site the query keeps to (category slugs), when it was read for them (readCategories).

excludeCategories.description: The kinds of site the query leaves out (category slugs), when it was read for them (readCategories).

understood.description: How the query was read, as far as ignore can change it (null: read as written).

title: Sections like these
